name: Marshfield
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Marshfield, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Marshfield, MA: the drive-through Celebration of Lights at the fairgrounds and the Christmas Show House at the Daniel Webster Estate.
lede: Marshfield's biggest holiday draw is the drive-through South Shore Celebration of Lights, with more than a million LEDs on the fairgrounds, and the Daniel Webster Estate fills December with its Christmas Show House, where children under 12 get in free.
celebrates: Christmas in Marshfield starts before Thanksgiving, when Marshfield Merry All the Way shows off decorated trees at its Festival of Trees on South River Street and The Molly Fund lights the tree in Dandelion Park on Ocean Street. Merry All the Way also runs a Holiday Lights Tour of decorated homes. From late November the Marshfield Fairgrounds glow with the South Shore Celebration of Lights, a drive-through show run by Fiesta Shows. In December the Daniel Webster Preservation Trust opens its Christmas Designer Show House and hosts Santa's PJ Party, and the Ventress Memorial Library holds seasonal story and craft times for young children.
lastyear: Last season the Daniel Webster Preservation Trust held its 20th Christmas Designer Show House, and Santa's PJ Party at the estate, a drive-up visit run every year since 2020, again welcomed more than 120 children to see Santa on the veranda while collecting food for the Marshfield Food Pantry. In November, Marshfield Merry All the Way opened the season with its Festival of Trees at 76 South River Street, raising money for local charities.
facts: Marshfield was settled by families from Plymouth Colony and became a town in 1640. Daniel Webster, the senator and Secretary of State, bought a farm here in 1832 and called himself the Farmer of Marshfield. His love of farming inspired townspeople to start what became the Marshfield Fair, whose fairgrounds now hold the holiday light show. John James Audubon visited Webster and painted wildlife in Marshfield, and part of the old Webster land now belongs to Mass Audubon.
trains: Marshfield has no commuter rail station of its own. The nearest stop is Greenbush, the last station on the MBTA Greenbush Line from South Station, in neighboring Scituate, and the Kingston Line ends at Kingston, to the south. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs its train through the Christmas lights each season, and Cape Cod Central Railroad runs trains from Hyannis. The Old Colony and Fall River Railroad Museum in Fall River keeps regional rail history on display.

kidfact: Daniel Webster, a famous senator, lived on a farm in Marshfield and liked to call himself the Farmer of Marshfield. The Great Linden Tree on his estate has been listed as the largest English linden in the country.
faq: When is the Marshfield light show open?

The South Shore Celebration of Lights runs at the Marshfield Fairgrounds from the day after Thanksgiving to December 30 on select nights. Hourly entry sessions run from 5 to 9 pm, with last admission at 8:15 pm. It is closed some Monday and Tuesday nights early in December, so check the schedule before you go.
How much does the Marshfield light show cost?

Tickets are sold per car, not per person. Online prices are $22.99 on weeknights and $26.99 on Fridays, weekends, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, and gate prices are $30 and $35. A $30 flex pass covers any open night, and buying online is recommended because gate sales stop if a night sells out.
Is the Daniel Webster Christmas Show House good for kids?

Children under 12 get in free, and families can walk through the historic Webster house decorated for Christmas. Adult tickets are $15 and seniors pay $10 at the door. The Show House runs for 11 days in mid December, with late openings until 9 pm on two Thursdays and two Fridays.
Where can kids see Santa in Marshfield?

The Daniel Webster Estate holds Santa's PJ Party, a drive-up visit where children step out of the car and meet Santa on the veranda. Families are asked to bring kids' favorite foods, such as cereal, juice boxes and pasta, for the Marshfield Food Pantry. The estate says more than 120 children come each year.
Can we take the train to Marshfield?

Marshfield has no commuter rail station. The nearest stop is Greenbush in neighboring Scituate, the end of the MBTA Greenbush Line from South Station in Boston. From there families finish the trip by car or rideshare. Kingston, at the end of the Kingston Line, is another option to the south.
